_about: Charts for the Before the classroom page. Each chart lists its records; a record with verified false or value null renders as pending with the placeholder badge. Checked 2026-11-21.

charts.title: Low-income students are underrepresented in computer science classes
charts.measure: Low-income students as a share of each group

records.metric: Students from low-income families as a share of all students
records.source: Alyson Klein, "One Change That Can Get More Girls, Students of Color Taking Computer Science," Education Week, Oct. 22, 2024, citing Code.org's 2024 State of CS report
records.notes: Article text: 'Students from low-income families comprise 53 percent of students but make up 38 percent of those in foundational computer science courses.' The article says 'students', not 'high school students'.

records.metric: Students from low-income families as a share of students in foundational CS courses
records.source: Alyson Klein, "One Change That Can Get More Girls, Students of Color Taking Computer Science," Education Week, Oct. 22, 2024, citing Code.org's 2024 State of CS report
records.notes: Same sentence as above. The article does not give the number of reporting states for this figure.

charts.title: Access to computer science at school, 2015 and 2025
charts.measure: Share of schools offering computer science

records.metric: Share of schools offering computer science
records.data_year: 2014-15 survey of U.S. K-12 principals, students and parents
records.source: Google and Gallup, Searching for Computer Science: Access and Barriers in U.S. K-12 Education, 2015
records.notes: Candidate figures, not yet chosen: 'Of all principals surveyed, three in four report that they do not offer computer science with programming/coding.' Also: 'approximately 25% of seventh- to 12th-grade students report having no access to a computer science class or club at school.' Both are survey responses covering K-12 schools, not a count of public high schools.

records.metric: Share of U.S. public high schools offering foundational CS
records.source: Code.org, CSTA and ECEP Alliance, 2025 State of AI + Computer Science Education
records.notes: The 2025 report gives 60% of public high schools offering foundational CS (verified on the home page). It is left pending here because it measures something different from the 2015 survey; a fair comparison needs the same measure in both years, for example an earlier Code.org State of CS figure. The 2025 report's own trend chart starts at 47% in 2019-20.
